newsitem.title: USA: RightChoice shares off on halted BJC talks.
newsitem.headline: RightChoice shares off on halted BJC talks.

text.p: Shares in RightChoice Managed Care Inc fell sharply after the company said it halted talks on a possible combination with BJC Health Systems, a St. Louis-area hospital organization.

RightChoice shares were off 4-1/4 to 12-5/8. They had run up after reports of the BJC talks surfaced in November from a 52-week low of 8-7/8. RightChoice acknowledged the BJC talks were occurring in January, said a company spokeswoman.
"We're disappointed that this (the BJC combination) couldn't happen," said Bill Nasgovitz, president of Heartland Advisors, whose Heartland Value Fund owns a RightChoice stake.
"We're long-term holders. We're sticking with it and if it comes down much more, I'll buy some more," he said.
RightChoice is the for-profit subsidiary of Blue Cross Blue Shield of Missouri and is that state's largest provider of managed healthcare services.
